environment.description: Same ECS Fargate task and code deployed in production account 444455556666. The Lambda function URL serving as the webhook ingress has AuthType=AWS_IAM configured. The resource-based policy on the function URL grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl only to principal arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/PartnerWebhookRole which is an IAM role in the partner's account that they assume via STS with ExternalId. Unauthenticated HTTP requests to the function URL receive HTTP 403 {"Message":"Forbidden"} before the Lambda code executes, so no SQS messages are enqueued from untrusted sources. Additionally, the SQS queue has a resource policy restricting sqs:SendMessage to the Lambda execution role only (arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/WebhookIngestLambdaRole), preventing direct queue injection. The gRPC downstream runs Istio 1.19 with STRICT mTLS and an AuthorizationPolicy that drops requests carrying x-internal-auth-principal metadata unless the source principal matches spiffe://cluster.local/ns/orders/sa/order-consumer.

config.lambda_resource_policy: Allow lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl for arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/PartnerWebhookRole with StringEquals aws:PrincipalExternalId=ptnr-8f3a2c
config.grpc_service_mesh: Istio 1.19 STRICT mTLS with AuthorizationPolicy on OrderService
config.network: Private subnets only, VPC endpoints for SQS
